topics.title: Start here
topics.body: The Android companion is for the household librarian. Pair it with your Windows, Linux or Raspberry Pi server using Paired admin phones. Borrowers use Create account / Sign in on the shared library page; they do not need the admin companion. The server must remain on and reachable.

topics.title: Administrator dashboard and navigation
topics.body:
The admin web dashboard and paired iPhone/browser companion have a responsive layout. Desktop uses a stationary left menu; on phones use Home, Catalog, Borrowers and More at the bottom. Catalog remains the initial view in this iteration. Home opens the whole-library dashboard. Its counts include all active collections, unlike a filtered catalog. Available excludes copies on loan and held copies. Recent requests includes resolved history; Active requests counts only pending and approved requests.

Quick Actions are Add Book, Create Hold, Batch Checkout and Backup Now. They open existing workflows; Backup Now opens backup options and does not create a backup until you choose and confirm an option. A hold does not start a loan. Confirm handover only when the borrower receives the books. System Status shows connection and links to the existing device, backup and reminder checks; the links do not mean a backup or delivery succeeded.

More / All tools keeps printing, numbering, requests, holds, accounts, reading, sharing, exports, recovery and setup available. Library settings retains your saved name, custom icon, sayings and colors. The sidebar repeats your existing encouraging saying; leave it blank in Library settings to hide it. Sidebar artwork opens a PNG upload and Remove artwork option. There is no built-in decoration. Upload your own PNG under 10 MB; recommended size 512 × 256 pixels with transparency. Larger images are fitted without cropping. The saved result is limited to 350 KB and is included in library exports/backups. Removing it clears it for this library and paired browser companions. Artwork never blocks controls and is hidden on narrow or short screens. Borrower pages and the native Android layout are unchanged in this first redesign iteration. Paired devices keep their existing authentication.

On desktop, the search box at the top searches the catalog: type a title, author, series, ISBN or copy ID and press Enter. The dashboard uses your saved library name, subtitle, icon and color theme; it does not install Queen B branding for other households. Sidebar artwork remains optional and is uploaded separately in Library settings. On phones Quick Actions follows Recent requests, while Home, Catalog, Borrowers and More stay reachable at the bottom. Native Android keeps its existing native screens.

topics.title: Borrower app: Catalog, My reading, My loans and Account
topics.body:
After an approved borrower signs in, Catalog opens first. Search and browse books, request an available copy, or open About this book. On phones use Catalog, My reading, My loans and Account at the bottom; on larger screens the same navigation is above the content. My account in the header also opens Account. Your current search stays when switching views.

My reading is your encrypted personal TBR/history. If it is locked, unlock it with your private passphrase or cancel and continue browsing. The separate passphrase is not required for catalog browsing or borrowing requests. Account → Private reading & wishlist has lock/unlock, private wishlist, clear finished reading and encrypted personal export/restore. Personal reading remains private from the librarian; operational library loans and requests remain visible to them.

My loans includes My book requests. Open requests have a count in the navigation. Request cancellation still requires confirmation and releases only its own hold; librarian approval is not a checkout. Refresh reloads the current state without changing views. Account contains install/Home screen, optional due-date notifications, account help, Data & privacy (clear completed history and account deletion) and Sign out. A pending account can still use install/help, sign out and its deletion tools before approval. Native Android administrator layout is unchanged by this borrower web/PWA iteration.

topics.title: Borrower account deletion: which username to enter
topics.body: In the borrower web/PWA, open Account → Data & privacy → My data & privacy → Delete my account. Choose the data scope and preview it. The confirmation field shows the exact sign-in username separately from your display/reader name. Type that sign-in username; the borrower page ignores capitalization, surrounding spaces and one optional leading @. It does not autofill the confirmation. Your current password is still required, with its exact capitalization and spacing. Changing deletion scope clears the username/password fields and requires a fresh preview. A different username, wrong password, stale preview or protected active loans still prevents deletion. Administrator account-deletion tools retain their own existing confirmation rules.

topics.title: Optional sidebar artwork
topics.body: No bottom/sidebar illustration is hardcoded or enabled by default. Open Library settings → Sidebar artwork (also under All tools), choose your own PNG, review the preview and Save artwork. Recommended canvas: 512 × 256 pixels; transparent background works well. Input must be under 10 MB and at most 8192 pixels per side. The app fits it without cropping and saves a bounded PNG. Remove artwork leaves the sidebar undecorated. It is shared with paired browser companions and included in library backups, independent of your library logo, colors and encouraging saying. It is decorative only and cannot cover buttons; narrow or short screens hide it. Native Android has no desktop sidebar.

topics.title: Local administrator sign-in and recovery
topics.body:
Carribrary now requires its own administrator sign-in on the server computer, even when Windows is signed in. This protects the local dashboard and administrative API. An update keeps your books, borrowers, settings and approved phones. Already paired Android and iPhone/browser companions keep their existing access without another password screen. Borrower sign-in and private reading-vault credentials are separate.

On first open, choose an administrator username and a password of 12–128 characters. The page shows the private local-admin-setup.txt file location in your server data folder. On Windows, select Start → Carribrary → Administrator access and approve the Windows administrator prompt; Copy setup code, then Open local sign-in. The installer also offers this private code when you finish and open the library. This helper only reads an existing code; it does not reset credentials or sign you in. Alternatively open the file using an authorized server administrator account. Paste the code into the setup form and confirm your password. Being the first visitor to the page does not grant administrator access. Do not send the setup code, password or recovery code to support.

Save the new recovery code privately, preferably away from the server computer, then select I have saved this code safely → Open library. Signing out ends this local browser session. Local sessions expire after 30 minutes idle, eight hours total, or a server restart. A fresh private/InPrivate browser must sign in independently.

If you forget your local password, select Recover local administrator access and enter your saved recovery code with new credentials. This consumes the code, creates a replacement recovery code and signs out all local dashboard sessions; existing paired phones stay approved. It does not reset borrower passwords or unlock private reading vaults. If every recovery code is lost, stop Carribrary and run the included server executable with --prepare-local-admin-recovery using the same data-folder configuration. This advanced, stopped-server procedure writes a new private one-time code without deleting data. Restart, open local recovery and use the code. The procedure is blocked while that data folder is in use. Never delete the credential file as a recovery method. An already authorized companion can also prepare a setup/recovery code through the protected server operation; a dedicated companion recovery button is not yet supplied in this repair pass.

Revoking a phone or paired browser rejects its next server request immediately, including requests on a reused connection. It does not erase a previously downloaded offline catalog. Disabling an account, local sign-out and unpairing a device are distinct actions.

The local dashboard uses loopback HTTP only; its HttpOnly, SameSite session cookie is not a public HTTPS companion credential. Do not forward its port or put it behind a public proxy. Public and native companions retain their existing secure connections. The multi-administrator update safely upgrades the protected credentials while keeping your original username, password and recovery code. Earlier programs cannot decrypt the new credential format. Program-only recovery is restricted to 2.0.36; keep a complete pre-update backup for supervised recovery to an earlier release. Retain complete private backups and use supervised recovery across this security boundary. On Flatpak, Stop server now opens the local browser, requires login if needed, and asks you to confirm stopping before shutting down.

More than one person can sign in. Open All tools → Dashboard accounts → Add administrator. Each person has their own username, password, recovery code and local sessions. All dashboard administrators have full library-management privileges, including managing additional administrators; add only trusted people. The primary account cannot be removed, and you cannot remove the account you are using. Up to 100 dashboard accounts are supported. Accounts can use different browser profiles or private windows simultaneously. On a shared browser sign out before another person signs in.

Give a newly created administrator their username, initial password and one-time-displayed recovery code privately. They can choose Change my password after local sign-in using their current password. It renews that session and ends their other local sessions. Reset password or Remove administrator immediately ends the affected account’s local sessions; other administrators stay signed in. Additional administrators can recover their own account with their username and recovery code. Primary account/server-owner recovery still ends all local sessions. Dashboard account removal does not delete a borrower/reader or revoke independent paired-device tokens; revoke those separately under Paired phones / iPhone companion. Borrower sign-ins never grant admin access. Existing paired companions keep token access without another password login.

topics.title: Complete server data backup — recommended before updates
topics.body:
On the server open Backups → Create complete backup. On Android open More → Settings & backups → Complete server data backup. The iPhone admin PWA uses the same server Backups dialog. Choose a backup password of 12–128 characters, confirm it, and save the .carribrary-backup file. Keep the password safely and store a copy on another drive. It cannot be reset. The server briefly pauses changes, captures consistent SQLite snapshots including committed WAL data, then resumes automatically; you do not have to stop it or copy hidden folders. Confirm that the download finishes before closing the page/app. Use the server computer for large archives.

Includes current library/loan records, borrowers, sign-in accounts, encrypted borrower vaults, pairing identities, keyring, notification/reminder saved settings and saved application configuration. Complete snapshots contain private records and server credentials, so they are password-encrypted. Borrower private reading stays encrypted inside the archive and still needs each borrower's own private passphrase/recovery code. This does not give administrators access to borrower personal reading.

Current-data limit: 2 GB and 10,000 files. Earlier automatic backups/recovery points, program binaries/installers, external HTTPS/Caddy certificates, operating-system service/task definitions and settings supplied only through environment variables are not included. Keep those separately if needed. This is a complete current server-DATA backup, not a full computer image or guaranteed cross-platform migration. Windows DPAPI-protected keys/settings require the same Windows computer.

The smaller Backups → Export library JSON option includes books and administrative lending records, but excludes credentials, pairing keys and borrower private vaults. Restore library export accepts that JSON only. It cannot restore a complete encrypted server-data archive.

Complete recovery is currently an offline utility, not a live browser restore. Stop Carribrary, keep the current data folder separately, then use the included HomeLibrary.Server --unpack-complete-backup ARCHIVE NEW-FOLDER command. It asks privately for the backup password, verifies authenticated encryption, inventory hashes and SQLite integrity, and unpacks only into a new folder. It never overwrites an existing folder or running library. Follow RECOVERY-READ-ME.txt in the recovered folder: restore the entire data folder together, including all databases/keyrings; use matching or compatible server programs; review supplied configuration separately. Get recovery help if unsure. On Flatpak, use the bundled Linux recovery instructions to grant access only to the archive/output folders for this offline command. Never put the backup password in a command argument or send it to support.

Copies outside Carribrary and downloaded archives can retain information deleted later. Keep these backups private and remove unwanted copies yourself. Forgotten archive passwords cannot be recovered. If a download fails, delete the incomplete downloaded file and retry. Internal temporary snapshots are removed after delivery or normal failure; a machine crash can leave an unfinished .complete-backup-* folder inside the protected data folder. Stop the server before cleaning up those unfinished temporary folders.

If a borrower still has legacy private reading records awaiting encryption, complete downloading is blocked until that borrower finishes private-list encryption setup. This avoids exposing legacy personal notes through an admin download. Ordinary library JSON export remains available and continues to omit those records.

Restoring an earlier complete snapshot rewinds account deletions, passwords, device revocations and lending history. Review accounts and paired devices before making the restored server reachable. Compatible program-only recovery keeps current data instead.

topics.title: Permanent copy identity and upgrading to 2.0.31
topics.body:
Each physical copy has a permanent internal identity separate from its visible BK catalog number. Editing, restarting, current-format backup/restore and Recycle Bin recovery preserve it. Reusing an available BK number creates a distinct copy identity. The optional QR labels use this permanent identity; ISBN/EAN and manual circulation still work without labels.

Before updating, create a complete private backup. The new server migrates library format 1 or 2 to format 3 and saves an encrypted pre-change administrative library backup. That administrative export is not a complete account/key/vault backup. Existing identities and numbers stay. Older JSON exports can be imported; identities absent from them cannot recreate original identities they never contained.

Versions 2.0.30 and earlier cannot open the upgraded library. Do not downgrade. Windows program recovery supports 2.0.36–2.0.37 multi-administrator credentials only; earlier programs cannot read the upgraded protected credentials and cannot be offered for program-only recovery; old private recovery points remain retained but cannot be offered across this data-format boundary. Cross-format recovery requires supervised use of a complete pre-upgrade backup. Update the server first, then companions; pairing remains valid.

topics.title: Home Library is now Carribrary
topics.body:
Carribrary is the new product name for Home Library. Install the new server and companion updates over your existing versions; export a backup first and update the server before the phone app. Do not uninstall or clear app data. Your library name (such as Queen B’s Library), books, borrowers, accounts, holds, reading lists, custom icon, settings and phone pairing remain yours. The existing book-and-house symbol is still the app icon; launcher labels, installer names and help now use Carribrary.

Windows updates reuse the registered install folder and replace the old desktop, Start menu and startup shortcuts. Windows Services shows Carribrary with the internal name HomeLibraryNative. Android keeps the same application ID and signing identity, so the APK updates the existing app. Linux keeps the same Flatpak ID and stable branch; Raspberry Pi keeps the home-library-server package and home-library service. Existing technical file names, data folders, scheduled task names and connection protocols may still contain Home Library or home-library for compatibility. There is no need to move data or pair again.

Browser apps keep your library’s own name and custom icon. Reopen or refresh after updating the server. Installed Home-screen labels and icons may take time to refresh; if needed remove only the shortcut and add it again. Never clear app storage merely to refresh an icon.

topics.title: Find your way around
topics.body: Catalog lists books. Loans shows checked-out copies. Reading has personal reading lists. More groups People & lending, Sharing & collections, and Settings & backups. Tap a group to expand it. Help is always available in the top banner.

topics.title: Add books and find covers
topics.body: Catalog → Add book → scan the existing ISBN or enter it → Look up book details → check the title, author and collection → Save. For missing images use Search Books for a cover. Review different-edition suggestions, choose Use this cover, then Save. Google Books is optional and configured in the server’s Library settings. Provider errors may require another try.

topics.title: Scan, check out and return
topics.body: Use the book’s printed ISBN barcode, an optional BK copy label, or manual entry. Checkout selects an available copy; return selects a checked-out copy. When several copies match, choose the correct one. Choose the borrower and dates, then confirm. Custom labels are optional. Reading status does not check books out or return them.

topics.title: Camera trouble
topics.body: Allow camera access when prompted. Choose the rear camera that focuses best and save it as the default. Use steady light, keep the barcode flat and move the phone slightly farther away. Manual ISBN/copy-ID entry always works. The server must use HTTPS for browser camera access.

topics.title: Borrowers, requests and receipts
topics.body: More → People & lending → Borrowers adds people you lend to. Requests go to the inbox for review. Approve a request, then hand over/check out the book when ready. Approval alone does not create a loan. Borrowing receipt prepares a text or email in your messaging app; you choose whether to send it.

topics.title: Reading lists
topics.body: Admin Reading manages household profiles that are not linked to borrowers. Those household profiles are shared with paired admins. Borrower personal reading, ratings, dates, notes, TBR and private wishlists use the borrower account’s encrypted vault and are not visible or editable in admin screens, phone snapshots or administrative exports. Borrowers use their account in a browser/PWA. Reading status remains independent of lending. A private reader can keep encrypted book details after a catalog copy is removed; a reused Copy ID with a different ISBN does not attach the old notes to the new book.

topics.title: Library QR, personal QR and accounts
topics.body: Share library / QR opens the public catalog. Guests can browse and request without an account. Accounts are needed for borrower-private lists: the librarian approves the operational borrower link, but the borrower sets a separate private-list passphrase and recovery code. Admin pairing QR codes grant library administration, not decryption of borrower personal records. Personal reading links for admin-managed unlinked household profiles remain capability links; anyone with such a link can use that household list, including an admin who issued it. Older borrower reading QR links no longer open borrower personal records; use a borrower account instead.

topics.title: Approve and recover an account
topics.body: Approve pending borrower accounts and link the correct operational borrower, or create one. Account sign-in recovery and private-list recovery are separate. A librarian can issue a one-use, 30-minute password-reset link after private reading is encrypted; it restores sign-in only, not the private-list passphrase or recovery code. Reset links are blocked while older personal records await encryption. Existing reset tokens and sign-in sessions are revoked once on upgrade to the new privacy model. There is no automatic email recovery service. An existing private profile cannot be assigned to a different account. If a deleted account’s borrower is approved for a new account, the new account starts a fresh private profile and does not inherit the previous private list; the owner can restore an encrypted personal backup with its own passphrase or code. When reapproving an existing account, select its correct operational borrower; its own hidden private profile stays attached to the same account. If the old borrower was removed and no replacement is selected, approval creates a replacement borrower. This does not unlock the encrypted list or transfer it to anyone else.

topics.title: Collections, filters and colors
topics.body: Catalog → Filter & sort reveals collection, sort order and page size. More → Sharing & collections manages collections. More → Settings & backups → Colors changes this phone’s theme. Library name & sayings changes the shared library banner. Collections organize books; they are not separate access-controlled libraries. The server’s Colors selector now saves the shared library palette, including borrower sign-in, registration, account and installed pages. On Android, Colors still sets your phone’s preference; Manage library → Use my colors for shared library publishes it to the server and borrower pages. Refresh open pages after a change. Legacy installations adopt the existing server browser’s selected palette when opened after updating.

topics.title: Backups, privacy and moving servers
topics.body:
Administrative Export backup includes catalog books, private shelf locations, Books to buy, borrowers, operational loans/requests and admin-managed household reading. It excludes borrower personal profiles, reading entries and encrypted vault contents. Keep this administrative export private: contacts and lending records still belong there. Administrative Restore preserves existing borrower private records rather than replacing them.

Borrowers use Export encrypted personal backup and keep the separate recovery code. A library JSON export is not a complete backup of sign-ins, pairing or personal vaults. For a complete host backup, stop the server and protect a copy of the entire data directory, including the account database, encrypted vault database and keyrings. On a new account/server, set up a new private list, then restore the owner’s encrypted personal backup using its original private passphrase or recovery code. Previous exports and safety backups may contain earlier unencrypted reading records; encryption cannot retroactively change existing copies.

topics.title: Offline, remote access and updates
topics.body: Offline mode shows the encrypted cached library; changes need a connection. Refresh after the server returns. Resolve Retry pending change before submitting another action. Remote browser accounts require your public HTTPS sharing address; no extra ports are needed beyond existing HTTPS sharing. Keep the server on. Install updates over the existing server/app, keeping data, rather than uninstalling first.

topics.title: Windows server: install, open and update
topics.body:
Install the Carribrary Windows installer on the computer that will hold your library. It runs the Carribrary service in the background and creates desktop/Start menu shortcuts. You do not need Node.js or a separate .NET installation. Open the Carribrary shortcut to administer your books. The normal admin address is http://localhost:4173 on the server computer.

Before an update, export a library backup. Run the newer installer over the current installation; do not uninstall or delete the data folder first. Close old manually started server windows so they cannot occupy the same ports. Install the matching Android APK over the existing phone app to preserve pairing.

topics.title: Start, stop and restart the server
topics.body:
Windows: open the Windows Services app, find Carribrary (HomeLibraryNative), then use Start, Stop or Restart. The native service is designed to start automatically with Windows. Closing the admin browser window does not stop it. If Windows reports a service error, use the installed diagnostics/repair tools and keep the diagnostic text for support; do not delete library data.

Linux Flatpak: launch Carribrary from the application menu. Closing the browser keeps the server running. The launcher’s Stop library server action stops it. Desktop logout or reboot also stops it; use desktop Autostart if you want it available after login.

Raspberry Pi: the DEB installs a systemd service named home-library. A desktop service manager can start, stop or restart it. The service normally starts at boot. Keep the Pi powered and connected while phones or borrowers need access.

topics.title: Linux and Raspberry Pi installation
topics.body:
Linux desktop: open the x86_64 Flatpak bundle in Discover or another Flatpak installer, then launch Carribrary from the application menu. Install Flatpak support through your software manager if needed. On a fresh install, log out/in if the menu entry is missing.

Raspberry Pi 4 or 5: use 64-bit Raspberry Pi OS and the ARM64 DEB package. Open it in the system’s package installer. The Pi version is the library server, not the Android APK. For remote administration of a headless Pi, use a secure tunnel or a local browser/desktop; the admin listener stays on localhost for safety.

Windows, Linux and Pi are alternative server hosts for a library. They do not automatically synchronize separate databases. Restore a library backup when intentionally moving records, then review phone pairing and account credentials.

topics.title: The three addresses: admin, phones and borrowers
topics.body:
Admin interface: http://localhost:4173 on the server itself. This address is for the server computer; localhost on your phone means the phone, not the server.

Paired admin phones: the configured HTTPS phone address, normally port 7443. Pair using Paired admin phones in the server UI and scan the private pairing QR. Approved phones administer the library.

Public catalog and borrower accounts: your configured public HTTPS hostname, normally port 443 through the public-sharing proxy. Share the library QR with visitors. They can create accounts, then you approve/link them. A personal reading QR is a different, private capability link. Never give an admin pairing QR to a borrower.

topics.title: Pair the optional Android admin companion — step by step
topics.body:
The phone companion is optional and grants administration of the library; borrowers use the shared library page instead.

1. During this preview, download the Carribrary Android APK on the phone, open it in Files and tap Install. Public releases are planned to use Google Play once the listing is available; no live store link is available yet. Only the APK goes on the phone; source archives and private signing folders stay off it. If Android asks, allow this installation from the app opening the APK. For updates, install over the existing app without uninstalling.

2. Keep Carribrary running on the server computer. For the first local test, connect the phone to the same home Wi-Fi/network as that computer. Guest Wi-Fi may block devices from reaching each other.

3. On the computer open Setup & updates and note a local phone address, such as https://192.168.1.50:7443. Use the actual address shown for your home network. For access away from home, finish the hostname/router setup first and use your configured HTTPS hostname and phone port instead.

4. On the computer open Paired phones at the bottom of the admin catalog. Enter that address in Phone server address and select Create pairing QR. Do not use localhost on the phone; it means the phone itself.

5. Open the Android companion, enter a Phone name, select Scan pairing QR, and allow camera access. Scan the PRIVATE QR displayed on the computer. It works once and expires after five minutes; create another if needed.

6. If scanning fails, use Copy private pairing text on the computer, transfer it privately to your phone, paste the entire text into Pairing code (manual fallback), then select Pair phone. Never post this text or the QR publicly.

7. Success: the phone says Connected to library server and shows the same catalog. If Offline appears, check the address, shared network, server power and firewall access to the phone port, then refresh. For remote access test again with Wi-Fi off. Keep the server running.

The public Share by QR code is for borrowers and cannot pair an admin phone. Revoke a lost phone from Paired phones. A normal update does not require pairing again.

topics.title: Remote access, DuckDNS and public sharing
topics.body:
The server needs a reachable HTTPS hostname for access away from home. DuckDNS points a chosen hostname to your changing home internet address; it does not itself install the library or provide HTTPS. Keep its IP updater running.

Don’t have a hostname? Create a free hostname at https://www.duckdns.org/, then return to Carribrary to finish setup. Sign in to DuckDNS using an available sign-in provider, choose an available subdomain, and copy the full hostname (for example, mybooks.duckdns.org) and your DuckDNS token into Windows Start → Carribrary → Connection setup. Select Save remote connection. Carribrary includes the updater and configures automatic address updates every five minutes; no separate DuckDNS application is needed. Keep your token private. If you already have a hostname and an updater, use those instead. For public browser sharing, select Set up public book-list sharing as well, then complete router forwarding and test from outside your home network. Creating a shared link alone does not configure DuckDNS or your router.

On Windows, use the installed Connection setup tools to configure the remote phone address and optional public book-list sharing. The public proxy obtains browser-trusted HTTPS certificates. Forward only the ports specified by your configured setup: public HTTPS normally uses 80/443 for certificate issuance and access; the paired-phone listener normally uses TCP 7443. Do not expose the localhost admin port or SQLite files.

Existing Linux/Pi reverse-proxy allowlists must include /s/*, /reading/* and /account/*, plus /robots.txt, to support all shared pages. Use the supplied Caddyfile example, validate and reload the proxy. If Wi-Fi works but mobile data does not, check DNS, router forwarding, Windows firewall, server power/network, and whether your ISP permits inbound connections. Tailscale is not required by this version. For the iPhone PWA add /companion/* to a restrictive proxy allowlist; the supplied Linux/Pi Caddyfile includes it. Windows public HTTPS forwarding already accepts it. Do not expose the private localhost admin port.

topics.title: Server data, backups and recovery
topics.body:
Export the administrative library backup before updates and regularly after catalog changes. It contains catalog/acquisition/location data, borrowers, loans/requests and admin-managed household reading, not borrower personal lists or vaults. Restore replaces administrative records and preserves current borrower-private records. CSV is a book list, not full recovery.

For complete installation recovery, stop the server and protect its whole data directory: borrower-accounts.sqlite, borrower-vaults.sqlite, library.sqlite and the remaining key/configuration files. Do not copy live SQLite/WAL files casually. Built-in library JSON/automatic library snapshots alone do not recover encrypted borrower vaults or credentials. Borrowers should also save their own encrypted personal export plus the separate recovery code. Windows machine-protected pairing keys can require re-pairing on a new host. Never share raw data/key folders as a public backup.

topics.title: Server troubleshooting checklist
topics.body:
If the admin page does not open, verify the service/Flatpak is running and open http://localhost:4173 on the server. A conflicting old server can block ports; stop the old process instead of starting several copies. If a phone goes offline, check that its saved server address is current, the server is on, and the phone is paired. Refresh after connectivity returns.

If public links show Not found, check that public HTTPS sharing is configured, the library link is enabled, the correct hostname is being used, and the proxy includes /reading/* and /account/* for newer features. Old personal links stop working after replacement or revocation.

If an account has no history, approve it and select the correct existing borrower/profile. If a book lacks a cover, use Search Books for a cover and review alternatives; provider outages do not mean your catalog is lost. For support, share the error message/version and sanitized diagnostics, never passwords, private QR codes, reset links or backups.

topics.title: Recovery and reused copy numbers
topics.body: Delete moves a book or borrower to the Recycle Bin. Open Recycle Bin from the server footer or Android More → Settings & backups. Restore returns the record. If an unreferenced book number has been reused, restoration assigns a free number and does not overwrite another copy. History-linked numbers stay reserved. Delete permanently removes the recovery option; records needed for loan/reading history stay archived. Recovery is included in library backups. Records permanently deleted before this update cannot be reconstructed by this feature.

topics.title: Bulk editing physical books
topics.body: On the server choose Select books, select individual copies or the current page, then Edit selected. Android has Bulk edit in Catalog. Choose up to 500 copies. Check the fields to change: collection, author, publisher or series. An empty checked text field clears it. Review the selection and confirm. Titles, ISBNs, copy numbers, covers, loans and reading history do not change. The entire edit fails without partial changes if a selected copy was removed or another client saved first.

topics.title: Automatic due-date email reminders
topics.body: Optional. Configure Email reminders from the server footer or Android More → Settings & backups. Use your provider’s SMTP STARTTLS host, usually port 587 (implicit TLS/465 is not supported), SMTP username, sending email and an app password. OAuth-only providers are not supported in this version. Save settings, send an explicit test to the sending mailbox, then enable. Edit each borrower and record their permission for automatic email. Valid email contacts only; phone numbers keep tap-to-send. One reminder is sent in the configured window before due, one on the due date, and one once the overdue threshold is reached. Returned loans are excluded. The server checks every 15 minutes after the configured start hour in its own time zone, and must be running. No due date means no automatic reminder. Sent means accepted by the provider, not guaranteed inbox delivery. Check-delivery may mean failure or interrupted delivery: check the mailbox before sending manually; uncertain attempts are not automatically retried. SMTP credentials and the delivery ledger stay separate from library exports, encrypted settings use the server keyring. Full private backups preserve them. Turning reminders off or clearing a borrower’s permission stops future sends. Changing a due date creates a new reminder schedule.

topics.title: Unblock and relink borrower accounts
topics.body: Unblock returns an account to pending and clears lockout; revoked sessions/reset links stay revoked. Approve it again for the verified operational borrower. The same account’s private profile is recovered automatically where it still exists. Restore a removed borrower or use the existing relinking options when appropriate. Re-registering a deleted username creates a new account with no inherited private access. To reconnect the old operational loan history, select the retained borrower rather than trying to claim the old private reading profile. Personal encrypted exports can be restored only by someone who has their private passphrase or recovery code.

topics.title: Setup checklist and safer updates
topics.body: Open Setup & updates from the server footer, Android More → Settings & backups, or the Windows Start/tray menu. It shows server version, private data folder, backup status, paired phones, addresses, port instructions and a DNS check. On Windows use Connection setup to save the hostname and DuckDNS settings; the wizard can open the router page and check DNS/local service. Reserve a stable LAN address. Forward TCP phone port (normally 7443), plus 80/443 only if public browser sharing is configured. Never forward admin 4173, internal catalog 4174 or discovery 7445. Test with Wi-Fi OFF; DNS/local checks cannot prove outside access or bypass ISP restrictions. Export a backup, install new Windows/Android versions over the old versions and keep data. Windows installer now stops the server and makes a complete private ZIP under the data folder’s parent/upgrade-backups before updating. The ZIP contains credentials and key material, is restricted to service/admin accounts, and must not be shared. These safety ZIPs are not automatically pruned. Do not use them as portable unencrypted public exports; Windows key protection can be tied to that computer. Linux Flatpak: quit the app and open the new bundle in your software manager to update. Pi: install the new ARM64 DEB; service data remains under /var/lib/home-library. No official automatic update feed exists yet. For 2.0.28 Windows setup, new core-library recovery points are stored in ProgramData/HomeLibraryNative/recovery instead; older upgrade-backups ZIPs remain separate. Use the Update and recovery topic for current behavior and cleanup.

topics.title: Deleting a borrower account and personal information
topics.body: Server: Borrower accounts → Delete account / personal information. Android: More → People & lending → Borrower accounts & approvals → Delete account / personal information. The same management flow is included in the iPhone source. Choose Sign-in account only to remove username/login credentials, sessions and reset links while keeping operational borrower, loan and request records. Both deletion scopes remove the account’s encrypted personal vault; it cannot be recovered by the librarian. Choose Account and linked personal information to permanently remove linked borrower/reader records, reading notes/ratings/dates, their requests, returned-loan history, and matching borrower Recycle Bin entries. Physical books stay in the catalog. Full erasure is blocked until active loans are returned. Account-only deletion is allowed with active loans. For pending/unlinked accounts or old removed links, select an additional verified reader/borrower explicitly; no history is claimed by name or contact. The preview lists operational records; private reading content and counts are not shown to admins. Records tied to another sign-in account cannot be erased this way. Other guest requests with matching contact details are kept unless explicitly selected and re-previewed; shared contact details do not prove ownership. Type the displayed username exactly and choose Delete permanently. A changed account/library requires a fresh preview. This is permanent and bypasses the Recycle Bin. Sign-in usernames become available for new registration, which starts pending without inherited access. The normal Delete borrower action still uses the Recycle Bin and does not delete a sign-in account. Block/Unblock also keep records; they are not deletion. Optional backup cleanup removes ALL stored automatic library backups and matching Windows pre-update safety ZIPs in the installation backup folders, for the entire library, not just this person. Leave it off to keep backups, which may retain older information and can restore it later. No pre-deletion backup is made for full erasure. New scheduled backups use the current library. Library-owner exports, other backup systems, sent emails and offline device caches cannot be recalled; refresh paired devices and manage those copies separately. This is deletion of live application records, not a guarantee of forensic erasure of disks. Borrowers can ask the library owner for deletion using Help with my account on the shared sign-in page. On an admin phone, resolve Retry pending change before deleting an account. Successful deletion replaces that phone’s saved library cache with the returned current library. Other devices must refresh separately. If the connection drops during deletion, refresh the account list before trying again because deletion may already have completed. New administrator-protected Windows recovery points are separate from ordinary backup cleanup; remove them through Update and recovery if historical data must be cleared. For 2.0.28 Windows setup, new core-library recovery points are stored in ProgramData/HomeLibraryNative/recovery instead; older upgrade-backups ZIPs remain separate. Use the Update and recovery topic for current behavior and cleanup.

topics.title: Install the borrower app from Chrome / add to Home screen
topics.body: Borrowers can save the shared library as a Home screen app without installing the household admin APK. On an Android phone, open the usual PUBLIC library QR/link in Chrome. Tap Install / add to Home screen on the book list or borrower sign-in page. If Chrome offers the install prompt, confirm Install. Otherwise tap Chrome’s ⋮ menu → Add to Home screen → Install (or Create shortcut), then confirm. If the link opened inside a messaging app, choose Open in Chrome first. Open the library icon from the Home screen afterward. It opens in a separate standalone window when supported. Guests can still browse and request books without an account; signed-in, approved borrowers get their own loans, reading and requests. Installation never grants admin access or bypasses sign-in/approval. No APK, signing folder or private phone-pairing QR is needed. Use the public HTTPS sharing link, not the private paired-phone server address. The app remembers only the last shared catalog path on that browser, so launching can reopen the catalog or the signed-in account. Private reading links, reset tokens, contacts, passwords and API responses are not saved by this web app for offline use. Normal secure sign-in cookies still apply and sign-in can expire. The server and connection are required; if unreachable, a simple offline explanation is shown instead of cached private data. On a shared phone, sign out. If the owner replaces/disables a sharing link, ask for the latest QR; opening the new valid link updates the remembered catalog. Already-approved accounts may still sign in independently. Web app changes load from the updated server on reopen/refresh; Chrome controls installation availability and icon/name update timing. On iPhone, open the shared link in Safari and use Share → Add to Home Screen → Add. This borrower web app is separate from the native iPhone admin source project. The installed borrower app also works on iPhone: open the shared link in Safari → Share → Add to Home Screen. Borrowers do not need the native Android administrator APK. The icon and colors follow the library’s branding.

topics.title: About a book / short descriptions
topics.body: Choose About this book on a catalog card to open a popup. It shows the librarian’s description first; otherwise the server looks for a short Open Library description, then Google Books if its key is configured. The source/link is shown. Missing descriptions are normal; the librarian can add optional About this book text in Edit details (up to 4,000 characters). Manual descriptions appear in the shared catalog and backups. Keep private reading notes in the Reading tracker, not the public book description. Lookup sends only book identifiers to providers and may be unavailable; it does not change the book automatically.

topics.title: Brand your library with an icon
topics.body: Server: Library settings → Library icon → choose PNG, JPEG or WebP → Save library icon. Android: More → Settings & backups → Library name & sayings / Manage library → Choose library icon. The image is fit into square 192- and 512-pixel PNGs; PNG/WebP transparency and empty padding are preserved. To remove a white background saved by an older version, upload the original transparent image again; an already flattened image cannot recover its transparency. No graphics tools are needed. Use default library icon restores Carribrary branding. Maximum upload is 10 MB; use a simple image if the resized PNG is too large. The icon is public and included in backups. It appears in the library banner and manifests for borrower/iPhone Home-screen apps. Browsers control installed icon refresh; remove and re-add a shortcut if it keeps the old icon. Native Android keeps its signed Carribrary launcher icon.

topics.title: iPhone librarian companion (PWA)
topics.body: No Mac, App Store build or APK is required for this hosted iPhone companion. First configure the server’s public browser-trusted HTTPS address. On iPhone open https://YOUR-HOST/companion/ in Safari → Share → Add to Home Screen → open the new icon. On the server choose iPhone companion → Create private iPhone pairing code. Alternatively Android → Manage library → iPhone / browser admin companion. Paste that code or private link into the installed companion, give the device a name, then Pair this companion. QR pairing links also work; installing first avoids Safari and the Home-screen app using separate cookie storage. Codes work once, expire after 10 minutes, and grant full library administration for 30 days. Never share them with borrowers. Revoke lost browsers from the server/Android companion list; Sign out / unpair revokes this browser. After expiry create a new code. The public library QR never grants admin access. Android continues using its native app.

topics.title: iPhone scanning and connectivity
topics.body: Inside the iPhone PWA use Add book, Check out or Return → Scan. Allow camera permission and keep the entire ISBN barcode sharp. ZXing provides barcode/QR decoding when Safari lacks BarcodeDetector; it is bundled locally, with no scanner CDN or paid service. Existing ISBN/EAN codes and optional BK labels work; choose the physical copy if several match. Manual entry/search is always available. Save the camera that focuses best where the browser exposes several choices. The server must remain running and reachable. The iPhone PWA does not store private library records for offline use; reconnect and refresh. More library tools groups the admin controls; Help is in the banner.

topics.title: Optional borrower push reminders
topics.body: Borrowers sign into an approved account, then choose Enable due-date notifications and allow the browser permission. On iPhone (iOS 16.4+) first add the borrower page to the Home Screen and open that icon. Reminders are checked every minute while the server runs: once up to two days before the due date, once on the date, and once at least seven days overdue. Returned books are excluded. Turn off notifications on this device uses the same button; other devices keep their choice. Sign-out turns off this device’s subscription. Blocking/deleting an account removes its subscriptions. Push permission is separate from recorded permission for SMTP email; text receipts remain tap-to-send. Notifications are generic and contain no book titles, borrower contact info or reading notes. Open the account for details. Send a test notification uses the same generic reminder. OS settings, Focus mode, push-service outages or an offline server can delay/prevent delivery; notifications are a convenience, not a guaranteed reminder service.

topics.title: Optional admin request notifications
topics.body: In the paired iPhone Home-screen companion choose Enable request notifications and allow permission. Only new pending requests after subscribing are notified; no old inbox backlog. Checks run every minute and group new requests into one generic alert. Open the library to review the inbox; a notification does not approve, reserve or check out a book. Turn off notifications on this device or Sign out / unpair disables it. The server’s Library settings → Notification status shows counts and last delivery status without subscription secrets. Browser admin revocation removes its notifications. This release adds Web Push to PWAs; the native Android admin has separate optional background request alerts described below.

topics.title: Push services, privacy and advanced hosting
topics.body: Web Push uses the browser/OS service (Apple, Google, Mozilla or Microsoft). Subscription endpoints, public client keys and VAPID private keys are protected at rest on the library server; no provider account or SMTP setup is needed for push. The server sends authenticated empty messages; each service worker displays a generic alert. Push services can see endpoint and delivery timing, not book/reading details. The private key and browser pairing credentials are never exported with source/application packages or ordinary library JSON exports. Keep HTTPS and the server running, allow outgoing HTTPS to the push service, and include /companion/* and /account/* in restrictive proxy rules. Do not forward port 4173 or 4174 directly. No extra inbound ports are required. Delivery attempts are deduplicated; uncertain sends are not automatically repeated to avoid duplicate alerts. Email reminders remain independent and configurable.

topics.title: Android background request alerts (optional)
topics.body: More → Settings & backups → Library name & sayings / Manage library → Enable background request alerts. Allow Android notification permission if asked. Existing pending requests form the starting baseline; only later new requests trigger a generic alert. The native app checks its paired server about every 15 minutes using Android’s scheduler; power saving, low battery, force-stop, permission settings or an offline server can delay or prevent checks. This is periodic checking, not instant Web Push, and needs no PWA or Firebase account. Tap an alert to open Requests. Test request notification displays a generic local notification. Turn off background request alerts cancels the scheduled check and clears its seen-request hashes. Forget connection also disables alerts. No book title, contact or reading notes appear in alerts. The phone keeps only request-ID hashes for deduplication; the paired server’s private data stays protected by the existing encrypted app cache.

topics.title: Personal To Be Read (TBR) lists
topics.body: After sign-in Catalog opens first. My reading is second and defaults to TBR: Want to read and Currently reading. Set up/unlock the encrypted list before adding or editing personal reading. Choose a separate private passphrase, save the displayed recovery code somewhere safe, then confirm you saved it. Neither secret is sent to the server. Mark as read removes an entry from TBR while retaining encrypted history, notes and ratings. Lock private list before sharing a device. My private wishlist stores unowned-book intentions and notes encrypted too; it does not make a borrowing request or add to the librarian’s Books to buy. Catalog browsing, requests and borrowing history work while the private list is locked.

topics.title: Exclusive holds and physical handover
topics.body: A successful borrowing request reserves its specific physical copy while awaiting approval. Another borrower cannot request that held copy; other available copies of the same ISBN remain independent. Public catalogs show Available, On hold or On loan without borrower details. Approve keeps the copy held; it does not create a loan or due date. Server footer → Lending & holds, or Android More → People & lending → Lending & holds / batch lending, shows reservations. Ready for pickup / delivery keeps the hold. Confirm handover only after the borrower receives the book: choose the handover date and optional due date, then check out. An admin can create a hold for an active borrower even without a request or contact information. Release hold makes it available and declines a linked request. Borrowers can Cancel request under My book requests; they can cancel only their own open requests. Holds do not expire automatically in this release. Release a manual hold before deleting its borrower, or any hold before deleting the book.

topics.title: Batch checkout, batch return and lending limits
topics.body: Server footer → Lending & holds → Batch checkout / Batch return; Android More → People & lending → Lending & holds / batch lending. Scan existing ISBN/EAN or an optional copy label, or search by title, author or Copy ID. A unique scan adds that physical copy; choose among multiple eligible copies. Review the selected list and remove accidental scans. Checkout defaults to five books per batch for one borrower and a separate maximum of five total active loans per borrower. Lending limits / Limits can change each setting from 1 to 100. Multiple batches or single checkouts cannot bypass the active-loan limit. Lowering limits keeps existing loans. Borrowing limits do not restrict returns. Held books are handed over from Holds / Requests. Confirm that the borrower has received checkout books, enter dates, then confirm. The entire batch saves together: if any copy is no longer eligible or the limit would be exceeded, no book in the batch changes. Refresh and review before retrying. Android preserves interrupted operations for Retry pending change; do not start a different change until resolved.

topics.title: Circulation upgrade and older requests
topics.body: The 2.0.25 server adds a versioned reservation list and lending limits without changing existing Copy IDs, reading profiles, accounts or pairing identities. On first opening older data it creates an encrypted before-circulation-v1 safety backup. Existing open requests remain intact. For an available copy, an approved request receives the reservation before pending requests; otherwise the earliest request wins, with stable ID ordering for ties. Requests for already-loaned or removed books do not receive holds. Conflicting older requests are shown without reservation for admin review: release/decline the competing hold if appropriate, then Approve the chosen legacy request to reserve it. No request is silently checked out or erased. Install the matching server and app updates; an older server cannot enforce the new hold rules, so do not downgrade with current data. Library exports now include holds and limits and remain private. Full personal-information deletion releases holds connected to the erased borrower or selected requests; account-only deletion keeps library records and their holds.

topics.title: Admin personal reading profile
topics.body: The librarian can keep their own named, unlinked household reader profile in Admin Reading; no borrower sign-in is required for that admin-managed list. Other unlinked household profiles are also visible to paired admins. For a list private even from admins, use a separate borrower account and encrypted personal vault. Admins cannot assist by opening or editing borrower personal notes or TBR. They manage only operational requests, holds, loans and due dates. A request message is deliberately sent to the librarian; it is not an encrypted personal note.

topics.title: Clear completed history safely
topics.body:
Borrowers clear encrypted finished reading with the private-list controls → Clear private finished reading. Unlock first, review the count, then type CLEAR HISTORY. Only finished reading entries/notes/ratings are removed; TBR, currently reading, private wishlist and loan/request records stay. Use Account → Data & privacy → My data & privacy → Clear completed history separately for returned borrowing or closed-request history.

Admins clear only admin-managed household reading and operational completed loans/requests. Borrower personal content is neither previewed nor cleared through the admin history tool. Active loans/holds and open requests remain protected. Account/data deletion is a separate, explicit operation that can remove an encrypted vault without reading it. Old exports/backups and other device copies may retain prior data.

topics.title: Delete your own borrower account and linked data
topics.body: Borrower account/PWA → Account → Data & privacy → My data & privacy → Delete my account. Review the preview, enter the sign-in password and type the username exactly. Both deletion scopes permanently remove the account’s current encrypted personal vault, legacy personal reading entries and sign-in access, so export an encrypted personal backup first if wanted. Account-only deletion retains operational borrower/loan/request records and is allowed while books are outstanding. Full information deletion also removes associated legacy reading/profile records, returned loans and requests and releases holds; active loans must be resolved first. Physical catalog books stay. The librarian can delete an account and its encrypted vault but cannot view its personal contents. Already exported copies and older backups cannot be recalled. /account/delete-help supplies browser-only instructions.

topics.title: Clear downloads and thumbnail cache on a device
topics.body: Borrower browser account → Account → Data & privacy → My data & privacy → Clear downloaded catalog / thumbnails on this device asks for confirmation and clears only Carribrary-managed offline caches. It does not remove server books, reading history, credentials or another site’s caches. The current borrower PWA has no managed whole-catalog offline download yet; the control is ready for that feature. Browser-managed image storage can also be cleared in site storage settings. Android admin More → Settings & backups → Data & privacy / clear history → Clear downloaded library on this phone removes the encrypted catalog/sharing cache while preserving pairing and server records. Resolve any Retry pending change first; Refresh downloads the library again. Admins can clear server history, but cannot guarantee remotely wiping a borrower’s disconnected device. The roadmap includes optional whole-shared-catalog downloads with last-updated/stale-availability labels and bounded cover caching where source terms permit.

topics.title: Books to buy — private acquisition wishlist
topics.body:
Server footer → Books to buy, Android More → Sharing & collections → Books to buy, or native iPhone More → Books to buy. Scan the existing ISBN in a store or enter it manually, use Look up book details/Search Books for a cover, review the match and save optional private acquisition notes. No catalog number is allocated and nothing appears in the public catalog. Edit or confirm removal from the wishlist as needed.

After purchase choose Acquired — add to library, confirm that you own the physical book, choose a collection/location and confirm any duplicate-copy warning. Android currently adds to General; Edit book can move it afterward. Adding the physical copy and removing the wish happen together. A failed or conflicting save keeps the wishlist entry. A live server connection is required; no offline store queue is claimed.

topics.title: Private shelf locations
topics.body: Add/edit a physical book → Room, Bookcase, Shelf. All are optional, at most 120 plain-text characters each. Locations belong to the physical copy, so two copies can be stored separately. Admin catalog cards/search and request/hold details help the librarian locate a copy. Locations and acquisition notes are excluded from shared lists and borrower account book projections. They remain in administrative backups. An older client that omits location fields on an edit does not erase them.

topics.title: Encrypted personal lists, recovery and limits
topics.body:
Borrower personal lists use a separate private passphrase, never the librarian-issued sign-in reset link. Save the random recovery code when setting up encryption. Private passphrase/code and raw encryption keys are not sent to the server or saved in browser storage by Carribrary; the server stores ciphertext. Unlocking lasts on the current page; Lock private list, signing out, navigating away or reloading removes the session keys. Browser back/forward restoration reloads the account page. Use a password manager and lock your device.

Forgot the private passphrase? Unlock → Use my recovery code instead → enter the code and a new private passphrase twice. The existing recovery code remains valid. If both the code and private passphrase are lost, the librarian cannot recover the old personal list. Encrypted personal backups can be restored with their original passphrase or code after unlocking the current list; type REPLACE PRIVATE LIST to replace only personal reading/wishlist data. Backups do not include the recovery code. Account deletion removes the current vault. The encrypted document is bounded to 4 MB; this is a data-size safeguard, not a limit on the physical library. Conflicting saves from another device require reloading/unlocking rather than overwriting it silently.

Existing unencrypted account reading records are imported during explicit setup: the encrypted document is committed first, then current plaintext records and corresponding action receipts are erased. An interrupted migration can be retried after unlocking. Previous backups/exports/admin device copies may still contain the old plaintext. This feature cannot retract or retroactively encrypt those copies.

Protection is for personal contents stored on the server/backups and hidden from ordinary admin tools. Requests, sent messages, loans, due dates, account identity and service activity remain visible as needed. A server owner who changes delivered web code or a compromised device can capture future secrets; this browser-based design is not protection against an actively malicious host and is not an independently audited security product.

topics.title: Household readers and private borrower accounts
topics.body: Add reader creates an admin-managed household profile, without a borrower link. Admins can view and edit household reading. Approve a borrower account through Borrower accounts and select the correct operational borrower; any explicit transfer of a household profile must belong to that person. Borrower personal reading then uses their encrypted account vault, never the admin reading screen.

topics.title: Illustrated Quick Start — first book, loan and backup
topics.body: Server Help → Illustrated quick start opens quick-start.html with current example screenshots and short steps: install, connect, add a book, add an optional borrower, lend, return, back up and recover. Print / save as PDF creates a printable guide. The iPhone admin PWA has the same authenticated guide. Android/iPhone offline Help retains the text instructions. Images use fictional sample records, never your live library. Standard Windows data lives separately from the program; the installer does not require Node.js or .NET. LAN-only use needs no public hostname.

topics.title: Windows Update and recovery — keep current data
topics.body:
Windows Start → Carribrary → Update and recovery, or the tray menu, opens an elevated recovery tool independently of the main server. Create recovery point briefly stops the service and saves verified program/data archives, including accounts, encrypted borrower vaults, keys and configuration. Before a supported update, setup creates a protected recovery point and checks new program file hashes, service startup and catalog access. A failed compatible update attempts program recovery automatically. Select a previous point → Restore selected application → confirm to restore compatible server/tray files while retaining CURRENT databases, account deletions, encrypted private lists and connection settings. Integrity and startup/catalog checks must pass. A failed recovery attempts to put the previous running program files back; private snapshots remain. Recovery-attempt safety copies are retained but not offered as previous-version candidates.

This release supports program recovery within the compatible 2.0.36 multi-administrator credential cohort. Earlier programs cannot read the upgraded protected administrator credentials; 2.0.30 and earlier also cannot read the format-3 library. It never restores historical data as part of ordinary rollback, never crosses older privacy-format boundaries, and does not yet perform incompatible schema rollback. Complete data archives are retained for supervised disaster recovery; Windows key protection may tie them to this computer. The tool needs an intact Windows/PowerShell recovery environment and administrator approval; physical Windows service/UI testing remains required. Linux/Pi retain existing package updates and stopped-server backups; guided rollback there is planned.

Version 2.0.31 upgrades the library to format 3 to protect copy-number preferences. Only 2.0.36 multi-administrator programs are in the automatic program-recovery cohort. Earlier programs cannot decrypt the upgraded credentials. See Permanent copy identity and upgrading to 2.0.31 before updating.

topics.title: Private recovery points — storage and deletion
topics.body: Windows recovery points are stored under ProgramData/HomeLibraryNative/recovery with access limited to Windows administrators and SYSTEM. They include sensitive historical data; do not share them. They are on the same disk, not an off-device backup or portable catalog export. No automatic retention cleanup is applied in this increment. Check available storage. In Update and recovery → Delete recovery points, type DELETE RECOVERY POINTS to remove all installation-managed recovery points and recovery-attempt safety copies. This removes previous-version recovery; current live records remain. Normal library backup cleanup cannot delete these administrator-protected points. Account deletion removes current account/vault records, but older recovery points and externally copied backups can retain historical information until separately removed. Uninstall retains recovery points and data. Points cover the server/tray program and complete core library-data directory. The public HTTPS proxy’s separate certificate directory and Windows scheduled-task definitions are not archived by this increment; compatible program recovery leaves the current proxy/tasks in place. These points do not replace a full off-device installation/machine backup.

topics.title: Copy numbering and safe optional QR labels
topics.body:
Server footer → Copy numbering, or Android More → Settings & backups → Copy labels & numbering. Choose Fill available gaps (the existing default) or Always use the next number. This affects new additions only: existing books keep their numbers. Numbers still referenced by loan, request or reading history remain protected in this release. The next-number option uses the saved high-water mark, including earlier allocations. Old backups cannot recover allocation history they never contained. Changing this setting never renumbers the catalog.

Use Print copy labels on the server or Copy labels & numbering on Android. Search and select existing books, choose Letter 30 labels (Avery 5160 geometry) or A4 24 labels (63.5 × 33.9 mm), then choose the first unused label position, across each row then down. Up to 500 copies per batch. Print / Save PDF on the server; Save label PDF on Android, then open the PDF in your print app. Print at Actual size / 100%, with browser headers/footers off. Test alignment on plain paper first. No custom layouts, saved print history or unlabeled-only filter yet.

The new QR contains a permanent physical-copy reference, not a sign-in, public sharing link or pairing secret. It works locally with your connected library. Both checkout and return accept these QR labels, existing ISBN/EAN barcodes, old BK labels and manual entry. A retired copy’s QR will never select another copy just because its BK number was reused. A restored copy keeps its QR identity even if its visible BK number changes. BK-only labels identify the current number assignment; remove obsolete labels when reusing numbers. Labels are always optional.

topics.title: 2.0.34 help repair and compatibility
topics.body:
This update fixes the iPhone/browser companion Help button and full-help links so they stay within the paired companion. Open Help in the top banner, search the topics, or select Open full server help page. If help cannot load, refresh the companion and check that its server is reachable. The hosted PWA receives this repair when its server is updated; refresh/reopen it afterward.

Create a complete private backup first. Install server updates over the existing installation without uninstalling or clearing data. Existing approved companion authorization remains unchanged. Local credentials now support multiple accounts; see Local administrator sign-in and recovery. Library format stays 3. Windows automatic program recovery supports the 2.0.36 multi-administrator credential cohort; earlier programs cannot read the upgraded multi-administrator credentials and are not offered for program-only recovery.

topics.title: Cancelling requests and reading hold status
topics.body:
Under My book requests choose Cancel request, review the title and copy number, then Confirm cancellation. Keep request closes the confirmation without changing it. Repeated taps are disabled while saving. Cancellation releases that request’s reservation; it does not return a borrowed book or release somebody else’s hold. Request status refreshes on Catalog, My reading and My loans.

If someone else changed the library, Carribrary refreshes the state and keeps the error visible. Review whether the request is still open, then confirm again if needed. A closed request cannot cancel a later request on the same copy. Declining an open request releases its associated hold; another valid reservation can remain. Use the admin Requests and Lending & holds views to identify the relevant request. Clearing completed history is never required to cancel or decline normally. History clearing retains its preview and confirmation and protects active loans, valid holds, pending requests, unfinished reading and TBR.

topics.title: Registration protection for self-hosted servers
topics.body:
Librarian approval remains required. Built-in protections work without an outside service: registration allows 5 attempts per client IP per 15 minutes, sign-in 20, and password-reset submission 10. These budgets are separate. Librarian reset-link issuance allows 6 per minute. Existing per-account failed-login lockout remains. Rate-limit errors tell the visitor to wait; they do not identify which account exists. A shared public IP may share a budget. Use the supplied trusted local HTTPS proxy configuration; do not expose the internal catalog port.

Optional advanced setup: create a Cloudflare Turnstile widget for your library’s exact public hostname. Configure BorrowerSecurity__TurnstileSiteKey and BorrowerSecurity__TurnstileSecretKey through your service/container’s private deployment environment (the .NET configuration names are BorrowerSecurity:TurnstileSiteKey and BorrowerSecurity:TurnstileSecretKey). Restart the server. Keep the secret out of source code, browser settings, screenshots and public files. Service environments differ from a signed-in desktop user’s environment; use the service manager’s protected configuration. Environment-only settings must be configured again on a replacement server.

Both values blank keeps Turnstile off. With either value set, registration requires complete valid configuration and server-side verification. Missing, expired, reused, wrong-host or wrong-action proofs are rejected. Provider outages block new registrations with a clear message; they never silently bypass verification. Sign-in, existing accounts and core library administration do not require Turnstile. The registration form loads Cloudflare only when this optional protection is enabled and the invitation is valid. Your site key is public; the secret stays server-side. Keep a secure copy of deployment settings alongside your private backup instructions.
